body:
There is no independent objection in the material — the rival is the only pressure the account has faced — so any decision I make here rests on one round of challenge rather than on a view tested from several directions. With that caveat, here is what I would use, revise, leave open, and drop, and on what grounds.

I am taking up the rival's probe, with two revisions grounded in a fact both inputs underweighted: the person asking is one of the three flatmates, not an outside adviser. Every move proposed so far — the record, the check-in, the one-to-one — is a move made by a party to the dispute, and in a three-person flat there is no neutral facilitator available from inside. So the probe ('when we last disagreed about what we'd agreed, what did you think we'd agreed to?') should be asked with the asker's own recollection on the table at the same time, not held back as a benchmark, and it should be framed as a question about the agreements, full stop, asked of everyone identically. That framing also resolves a tension inside the rival itself: it criticizes the one-to-one approach, then proposes three one-to-ones. The criticism, accepted, was never really about privacy — it was about making the withdrawing person the subject of a conversation about their withdrawal. A uniform question about agreements asked of all three doesn't do that. On that ground I am dropping the account's opening move (asking the friend what makes these conversations costly) as a first approach, while keeping it available if the friend raises it unprompted.

I am revising the record rather than adopting or rejecting it. To be fair to the account first: it already reached for part of this with 'what done means,' and its own commitments treated the record as a test rather than a validated remedy. But done-ness is a completion standard, not a scope or recurrence statement, and the rival's best point covers more ground: a note reading 'A: dishes, Mon' says nothing about what 'dishes' covers or whether it recurs, so an under-specified record just relocates disputes onto interpreting the note. The rival also conceded it hadn't shown a record makes things worse. The resolution I propose is to demote the record from remedy to byproduct: if the probe shows the recurring disputes cluster on scope (what the task covers), recurrence (standing role or one-off), or timing (by when), each cluster has a narrow habit as its fix — state that one thing aloud at the moment of agreement — and the note's only job is to freeze what was stated. This makes the probe more diagnostic than the rival claimed: it doesn't merely weigh grand readings against each other, it selects which small habit to adopt.

I am leaving the standing-negotiation reading open, but giving it a signature rather than a verdict: if, after scope-stated agreements, the disputes don't fall but migrate — from who does what to who wrote the note, who called the check-in, who's keeping score — that weights the third reading. I would also revise the rival's script for that case. 'What is it protecting?' presupposes the rival's own reading and will sound alienating to a household that may simply be disorganized. The flatter 'we keep having this same disagreement — what is each of us actually disagreeing about?' works under all three readings. I don't claim the flat version will work; I claim it fails less badly.

Two additions neither input made. First, schedule churn breaks any system built on fixed standing assignments, and the two escapes trade off: standing roles save negotiation overhead but generate exactly the standing-role-versus-one-off ambiguity; per-cycle re-agreement removes the ambiguity but costs a weekly negotiation the avoidant friend may simply not attend. Which side to take depends on how the household weighs overhead against ambiguity, which the material doesn't say — though the probe's recurrence answers would inform it. Second, a possibility neither input would state plainly: the material shows the friend avoiding conversations the asker is in. That is not evidence the avoidance is about the asker, and I am not claiming it is; I am claiming the asker cannot rule it out from inside and should not design as if it were impossible.

Sequencing, then: probe first, because it is the only move that generates information without requiring the avoidant friend to attend anything or accept any framing; habits and the byproduct note second, chosen by what clusters; the weekly check-in kept only for its schedule-declaration job — stating changes before they bite — and never used by two flatmates to decide for three. If the probe cannot even be convened, if either flatmate declines a single low-stakes one-to-one, that failure is itself informative, and it is the natural point to consider some outside third party both trust. I have not specified who, because nothing in the material does.

What I am not doing: claiming any reading is right, claiming the household will formalize anything, or ranking a mediator above the asker's own moves. The probe's value is that one flatmate can start it this week without anyone first agreeing on what the problem is — which, given the avoidance, may be the only kind of move currently available.
commitments:
Taking this up involves several separable commitments.

A claim I am making that appears in neither input: the asker is a party, not a facilitator, and every proposed move therefore carries the asker's own standing into the room. Under the standing-negotiation reading, even initiating the probe is a move in the game being studied. I do not think this can be neutralized from inside; the most that can be done is to disclose one's own recollection alongside everyone else's. Anyone adopting the probe on my terms accepts that the initiator's asymmetry is owned, not removed.

The probe itself, as revised, is an application commitment: ask all three, including the asker's own account, the same content question, framed as being about the agreements. Its weaknesses I keep from the rival and do not claim to have solved: recollection is what is already in dispute, so the probe reaches current reports rather than past facts, and it may still be read as interrogation. Someone taking it up commits to accepting a non-clustering result without treating it as confirmation of the standing-negotiation reading — non-clustering underdetermines; it does not select.

On the record, I commit to the byproduct claim: an under-specified note carrying only task, person, and day is untested rather than an improvement, and any note kept must carry the scope, recurrence, and deadline stated aloud at the moment of agreement. This is falsifiable cheaply — if scope-stated agreements plus the byproduct note leave meaning-disputes standing on the same tasks, my demotion was wrong and the relocation critique applies to my version too.

On the standing-negotiation reading I commit only to its signature — dispute migration after the fix — and to watching for it, not to the reading itself. Someone observing migration should resist jumping to 'it's about status'; migration is consistent with other explanations, including a household where one system failure simply replaced another.

The revised script ('what is each of us actually disagreeing about') is a proposed utterance that inherits all the uncertainty above. If it lands as evasive or therapeutic, the commitment is to revise it again, not to read the flatmates' reaction as resistance.

Unresolved and not papered over: whether the avoidance concerns the asker; whether the household will formalize anything; the actual load distribution; whether the check-in can convene at all. If the probe is declined by anyone, I have committed to treating that as information — weighting either the standing reading or the possibility that the avoidance is personal — and to considering an outside third party at that point, but I have specified neither who nor whether one is wanted, because the material does not.

If this continues, what I would want reported back is whether recollections clustered and on what, and whether the avoidant friend answered the uniform question — not whether any of my preferred readings were confirmed.
